items.title: David Brinkley Interview, 1962-01-10
items.q: Men like Butter Petit, Chris Kelly, Sam Morgan, Celestan. You have a few left, but you could hardly, you've got to go all across the river, all Uptown, to try to assemble one good band now.

ctx.x: Where I can move, those love makes me great.

Blind Dee Dee Pierce and his wife, Billy, once considered New Orleans' greatest blues team, played together 27 years. Now play only when neighbors make requests over the back fence and they're on relief. Oh, well, well, that is with me everywhere I roam. George Gayno has played his banjo all over the world, but now, back home in New Orleans, he can't make a living. We asked George how many of the old-time jazz musicians were still around. Well, no, I believe there was a total, maybe not very long ago, in the…

Well, there were times that we put the music above the ring of the cash register, the tinkle of the ice and the glasses. There were many times, one in particular, when Papa Celestan played, he did a thing called Just Telephone Me with a tight mute in it. And no one served a drink, and the register didn't ring, and no one spoke, said a word. It was just about the same as being in the cathedral at high mass. We wanted the real thing, the genuine thing, and that's what we kept here for four or five years. The time…
